M3

Acceptance teardown can hang in the sandbox until the attempt timeout

First M4 live run (run 7b4961c8, 2026-08-30 18:33Z): both scenarios failed within 60 s, then Playwright's runner sat in epoll for nine minutes with No projects matched the filters in "/home/zaphod/work/rich" and next-server (v16.2.12) alive until the 600 s attempt timeout. On the host the same workspace exits in 39 s, so the hang is sandbox-specific (bwrap --new-session/--unshare-pid and Playwright's process-group kill of the web server are the suspects). A host-side reproduction inside the sandbox failed to launch Chromium (pthread_create EAGAIN) while another build was running, so it is unproven. Cost: ten minutes per failed acceptance attempt. Candidates: webServer.gracefulShutdown in the scaffold's Playwright config, starting next directly instead of through pnpm, a per-gate timeout below the task timeout.

Arbitrary-directory source read via path traversal, and no Host check at all — a DNS- rebinding hole. Both fixed, then the surface was deleted outright.

engine5b1b042

Architect always assembles

0/6 → 6/6 first-attempt, measured. Derive what the model already evidenced; drop the claim it cannot express; keep a valid answer in reserve.

enginebd3bd94

Durable cancellation

The engine always checked a token; nothing could set one. Now reachable from any surface, because the process that starts a run is rarely the one asked to stop it.

enginecc793de

Gate output feeds the retry

Redacted to what the failing task may read, so a diagnostic cannot leak a sibling's source. Evidence informs generation; generation never becomes evidence.

engineaefc481

Rebuild one node

Scoped per project; siblings replay from memo instead of being paid for twice.

engine03304fa

Generation memoized, verification never

Keyed on the exact request, so a retry — which carries its predecessor's failures — can never replay the answer that just failed.

engine3532017

Obligations are executed, not declared

Contracts compile to a vitest suite against a pinned interface and run as their own gate. Verified live: 9 property gates green.

engine4e62532

models split by subject

3,900 lines → six modules, one import name, acyclic and held to it by a test.

codebasee874f07

Names stop referring to a version that is gone

richbuild, command rich, API /v1, classes named for what they are. Wire-format strings deliberately untouched.

codebase3c968be

One product, not two systems

v1 engine, its surface, its half of the UI and the dead canvas importer removed. One server now answers the API and serves the canvas.

codebase3c968be

1.0.0, with a changelog

A version customers can pin and a record of what moved — naming the defect, not just the fix.

release75dbf3a

The rail says what is waiting on you

Derived from durable objects rather than a counter, so an unapproved spec no longer reads as a finished stage. Each stage jumps to its section.

canvasaaac89a

Contracts read as behaviour

Operations as signatures in words, obligations as the sentences they mean — each one compiled into a test that runs.

canvas7613c91

An architect's control plane, not a developer's

The run leads with an assurance panel: every requirement, its scenarios, the gates that spoke for it, proven or not. Source moved behind a disclosure labelled for audit.

canvas0b28a76

The blast radius is derived, not guessed

An implementation change cannot reach a consumer — none was ever shown it. A contract change invalidates consumers transitively. The firewall, cashed in.

engine58ac550

A change costs what it changes

Two approved revisions compile to the smallest stale set. Measured on a model-authored architecture: amending a UI-only requirement leaves data and domain replaying from memo.

engine58ac550

A protected input is context, not workspace

Compiled-from-intent modules were model-editable and shown as "your files" the parser would refuse to let it write. They also carried every capability, so amending any requirement changed every node's inputs.

enginee745bc1

Only remember what the gates accepted

The memo was written as soon as source applied, so a generation whose gates then failed stayed replayable. The worker now stages it and cannot commit it — whatever ran the gates does.

engine5cd675a

A retry asks, it does not replay

Fixing the key made every attempt replay the same rejected answer — three identical gate failures without ever asking the model.

engine00992ae

A repair's memo is still replayable

Its bundle says "replace" for files a fresh scaffold lacks. That guard protects against a model's mistake, not against replaying an already-verified answer.

engine07891fe

Keyed on the run's baseline

A failed attempt leaves its source behind to repair, so the winning answer was filed under "the workspace after a failure" — a state no fresh run reproduces.

engine3564984

The memo key is the question, not the coaching

Recorded under whichever attempt won — so any task needing a retry filed its answer under a key that could never recur. Memoization only helped tasks that succeeded first try.

engine92074d7

A failing check says what it got

Every generated assertion collapsed to a boolean before asserting, so a failure read "expected false to be true". The retry loop was working perfectly and being handed a message with no information in it.

engine344241c

One operations module per component

Every component's operations lived in one shared module owned by domain — so domain implemented accept_req_a11y, an operation belonging to app. Change locality was real at the contract level and worth nothing at the implementation level.

engine82b96cd

The verifier accepts idiomatic TypeScript

_input is how TypeScript says "deliberately unused", and the pinned interface makes it common. The lint gate was failing correct code for it.

engine6fc6019

A node is gated on its own contract

The property gate ran every contract's suite on every task, so domain failed because web — built later — had not written its module yet. A node was being judged by another node's absence.

engine635d6fc

Change locality, proven live · green

A standing test now: build, amend a requirement the domain layer does not serve, rebuild. Domain replayed its memo and passed every gate on its first attempt; web, which does serve it, was rewritten. Nine real defects came out of getting there.

engine6fc6019

Select the project, not just create it

"Create or select" could only create; a second project was reachable only by typing its id from memory.

canvasfb2e9bf

The CLI works where people type

rich serve --state-dir X answered "unrecognized". Found by installing clean and following the README.

release7a11ad1

Watch a run happen

rich logs --follow renders the durable events as a timeline. Evidence lines say what they spoke for.

enginec1be254

Provider conformance suite

Seven rules every adapter obeys, run against all three. Found a real bug on its first run: a cost ceiling of zero was constructible, authorizing a call with no money budgeted.

enginecec3beb

A failed attempt says why

"handler raised ProviderFailure" with the reason discarded — the event recorded the reservation, the usage and the retryable flag, but not what went wrong. Now a bounded reason, capped so a chatty upstream cannot push a response body into the event stream.

enginec6895d4

One route for designing and for building

The architect defaulted to the subscription route and the builder to the API one, so a host with a claude login could design an architecture and then fail to build it. Now one explicit choice, printed in the banner, still never substituted.

enginec6895d4

The architect was unreachable from the product

Driving it as a user: create, interview, approve, Draft → source: planner in 17ms. No model call. The feature measured at 6/6 was not wired into the only surface anyone uses — a regression from retiring the old canvas, which did wire it.

engine9188357

A slow step says how long it has been slow

Drafting an architecture is one bounded model call and takes minutes; the button said "Designing…" for all of them, indistinguishable from a hang. Now an elapsed count and an honest range — no progress bar, because RICH has no estimate and a bar over an unknown duration is a lie. Written blind during the tooling outage, then verified: typecheck, 667 tests, and a production build all clean.

canvas5e09f7c

Decided, and why

kept

models keeps its own path check

An explicit layering rule says it imports no sibling. Weakening that to fit a refactor was the wrong trade, so the duplication is intentional and says so in the code.

kept

The program's releases are 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2

v1.0.0 was tagged on 27 Aug on a tree a wheel cannot install. Rather than move a tag, the numbers move: the async operations interface, the new value kinds, new packs and new routes justify a major anyway. The changelog gains an Unreleased section; nothing that was tagged is rewritten.

reversed

Retiring v1 would have cost the canvas

The census said delete it. Acting on that would have deleted the React Flow canvas with it, so v2 got the graph first — then v1 came out having lost nothing.

kept

The architect's four-layer cap

It is a choice, not a limit — the compiler's ordering is general and would carry a deeper graph today. It is also what took first-attempt assembly from 0/6 to 6/6. Growth belongs at the pack boundary.

kept

The unwired OpenAI adapter

A seam with one implementation is not a seam. The conformance suite that proves the claim now exists (tests/test_provider_conformance.py, seven rules, three adapters, shipped cec3beb), so the adapter stays as the second implementation — wired to nothing, never a fallback.
